recent_posts.title: Using agentic coding to improve software quality instead of throughput
recent_posts.summary: Agentic coding (AI-assisted development) can improve software quality rather than just throughput. When code generation becomes cheap, previously uneconomical practices become viable: building custom tooling, prototyping multiple solutions to discover constraints empirically, implementing low-value-per-line abstractions like safe FFI wrappers, and aggressively paying down technical debt. Real examples include custom linters, safe Rust interfaces over C FFI functions, and migrating C code to Rust for better static analysis coverage. The shift enables quality-focused organizations to raise engineering standards by making verification infrastructure investments economically feasible.

recent_posts.title: biscotti, a new crate for HTTP cookies
recent_posts.summary: biscotti is a new Rust crate for handling HTTP cookies on the server side. It aims to provide a simple API for handling cookies while also covering more advanced cookie scenarios. The crate distinguishes between request and response cookies, provides centralized management of cryptographic guarantees, and supports rotating signing/encryption keys over time. The crate can be used alongside the cookie crate and is designed specifically for server-side cookie handling.

recent_posts.title: Rust web frameworks have subpar error reporting
recent_posts.summary: Major Rust web frameworks like Actix Web and Axum have subpar error reporting capabilities, according to the author. They discuss the limitations of error reporting in these frameworks and compare them to Pavex, a new Rust web framework that offers better error reporting. Pavex is highlighted as having the best error reporting story in the Rust web ecosystem.

recent_posts.title: This month in Pavex, #8: docs, docs, docs
recent_posts.summary: This post discusses the importance of documentation in a project and how Pavex tackled the challenge of creating comprehensive documentation. It highlights the use of the Diátaxis framework, the use of  `rustdoc`  and MkDocs for documentation, and the custom tool used to generate snippet files for the documentation. The post also mentions the priorities for the coming month, including stability, further documentation improvements, and conducting a gap analysis for existing projects.

recent_posts.title: Time to polish: Pavex is in closed beta 🎉
recent_posts.summary: Pavex is a one-stop shop for API projects, aiming to make Rust a mainstream language for backend development. It provides first-class solutions for common API development tasks and offers a smooth integration with high-quality third-party libraries. Pavex lowers the barrier of entry for Rust, catches errors at compile-time, and is designed to be flexible. To try it out, sign up for early access on the Pavex website.

recent_posts.title: Crafting boring APIs: lessons learned from implementing fallback handlers in Pavex
recent_posts.summary: Luca Palmieri has been struggling with Pavex, the Rust web framework I'm developing. A fallback handler is the function that will be invoked when an incoming request fails to match any of the routes you registered. All your routes expose a JSON-based API, but all your routes are serving HTML pages.
